title: Audit event slimline schema design and migration notes
content:
Purpose
-----
This doc is a working draft proposing a compact, low-cardinality audit-event schema (\"slimline\") intended for high-throughput SIEM export and long-term cold storage. Goal: reduce per-event size, minimize indexing cost in downstream systems, and maintain sufficient fidelity for security investigations and automated evidence automation. This focuses on mapping RBAC v2 concepts into a compact canonical event and describing a migration strategy/shim to preserve compatibility with v1/v3 exports.

Design principles (short)
- Minimal canonical set of fields required for triage and compliance: timestamp, actor-id, action-id, resource-id, outcome, trace_id (optional), evidence_refs (optional).
- Keep freeform attributes out of the core record; include a small compressed attributes blob only when necessary.
- Use stable short keys (1-3 chars) for exported lines to save bytes in Kafka/Firehose.
- Support two encodings: readable JSON for internal audit viewers + compact line format (pipe-separated or minimal JSON) for SIEM ingestion.
- Provide a compatibility shim service that expands or contracts attributes to match the target consumer schema (v1 verbose / v2 slimline / v3 enriched).

Why we need a slimline schema
- Hosted API and dedicated deployments generate millions of events/day. SIEM indexing costs are sensitive to field cardinality and event size.
- Current verbose schema (v1 style) duplicates large nested RBAC blobs and request bodies. That increases storage bills and slows search.
- We must still support incident workflows and evidence automation (e.g., attach precise request payload when legal/CS needs it) without storing that in every event by default.

Core canonical fields (proposal)
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp (string)
- eid: event id (uuid)
- aid: actor id (user/service principal; canonical format `u:<id>` or `svc:<id>`)
- act: action short token (see action token dictionary below)
- res: resource token (canonical path-like id)
- out: outcome enum (ok|fail|denied|error)
- rbac: rbac flavor token (v2) mapping (short encoding; see below)
- tid: trace id / request id (optional)
- ev: evidence refs (comma-separated small ids pointing to S3/KV)
- m: metadata blob base64(zlib(json)) — only when extra context is necessary (rare)

Action token dictionary (initial)
- auth.login => auth.login (act token: \"al\")
- model.invoke => model.invoke (act token: \"mi\")
- model.upload => model.upload (\"mu\")
- config.update => config.update (\"cu\")
- key.create => key.create (\"kc\")
- role.assign => role.assign (\"ra\")
- webhook.exec => webhook.exec (\"we\")

Resource token guidance
- Use compact path-like format: <kind>:<short-id> or <svc>/<resource> e.g., model:m-3b23 or project/p-12
- Avoid embedding large JSON in resource field

RBAC v2 mapping (compact)
- RBAC v2 introduces policies expressed as (subject, verb, scope, constraint). We encode the effect into a 1-byte token in the `rbac` field using the pattern: <version>:<effect-token>:<scope-hash-short>
  - Example: `v2:gr:s12` meaning RBAC v2 grant decision, short scope id s12.
- Store full policy references in evidence store (ev ref) only when the policy itself was the reason for decision (e.g., deny due to constraint).

Evidence automation hooks
- evidence_refs (ev) point to S3 object keys or an evidence index ID. Evidence store contains: full request body, full RBAC policy fragment, model response snippet, and supporting metadata.
- Evidence store lifecycle: TTL policy of 90d for default, extendable to 365d for legal holds.
- Automation consumer (forensics/e-discovery): when ev is present, a batch fetcher can rehydrate and re-run deterministic evals locally.

Encodings for export
1) Compact line format (preferred for SIEM high-throughput)
   - pipe-delimited single line: 
     ts|eid|aid|act|res|out|rbac|tid|ev|m
   - Example line: 
     2026-03-02T19:22:13Z|4f9b9a3f-...|u:1023|mi|model:m-3b23|ok|v2:gr:s12|t-9a8b|ev:idx-44321|
   - Downstream transformer can map to index fields and optionally expand `m` when present.
2) Compact JSON (for internal consumers + logging)
   - Minimal keys: {"ts":"...","eid":"...","aid":"...","act":"mi","res":"model:m-3b23","out":"ok","rbac":"v2:gr:s12","ev":"idx-44321"}

Migration strategy (v1 -> slimline -> v3)
- Provide a shim service at the export plane that takes the current verbose v1 events and emits slimline events downstream. Shim responsibilities:
  - map verbose RBAC structures to short rbac token and ensure policy refs are persisted in evidence store with index id (ev).
  - if `policy_debug=true` flag for a customer, retain additional fields in `m` compressed blob.
- Version negotiation: consumer declares desired export schema via header or topic name (e.g., audits.v1, audits.slim, audits.enriched.v3).
- Compatibility tests: create an integration test suite that validates lossiness is limited to non-essential fields and that reconstructable fields (via evidence_refs) suffice for audit.

Indexing and SIEM best practices
- Reduce field cardinality: map long user emails to stable short ids in `aid` (mapping table kept off-index).
- Avoid indexing `m` blob; only index top-level `act`, `res`, `out`, `ts`, `aid` for fast searches.
- For Splunk/Elastic: provide ingest pipeline that extracts `act`/`res` tokens into facets and drops unknown attributes.

Operational rollouts and telemetry
- Stage 1 (internal): emit slimline to a parallel topic (audits.slim.staging) for 2 weeks; collect diffs vs v1 and a set of replay queries.
- Stage 2 (partner beta): enable for a small group of customers; monitor false negatives in investigator workflows (i.e., ability to find necessary info).
- Stage 3 (GA): flip default for high-volume paths (model invokes, streaming) while leaving admin/identity events in verbose mode by default.

Open questions / TODOs
- Action token canonicalization: should we maintain human-readable fallback mapping inside the central schema registry? (likely yes)
- Scope-hash collision risks for `rbac` short scope ids — acceptable? Need collision window analysis and TTL.
- Encryption-at-rest and access controls for evidence store keys referenced by `ev` — confirm KMS+IAM pattern.
- Retention defaults: 90d vs 180d for EU customers; map to compliance profiles.

Example: compact event + evidence index entry (text)
- Slimline event (compact JSON):
  {"ts":"2026-03-02T19:22:13Z","eid":"4f9b9a3f-...","aid":"svc:ingress-4","act":"mi","res":"model:m-3b23","out":"ok","rbac":"v2:gr:s12","ev":"evidence-20260302-44321"}
- Evidence index entry (separate S3 JSON blob pointed to by ev):
  {
    "ev_id":"evidence-20260302-44321",
    "eid":"4f9b9a3f-...",
    "request_body_snippet":"{\"inputs\":\"...\"}",
    "full_rbac_policy_fragment":"{\"subject\":\"u:1023\",\"verb\":\"invoke\",\"constraints\":...}",
    "stored_at":"s3://redwood-evidence/2026/03/02/44321.json.gz",
    "retention":"90d"
  }

Notes to implementers
- File: platform/services/audit/exporters/slimline_exporter.go (pseudo) should implement streaming zlib(base64(json)) compression for `m` only.
- Add feature flag: audit.slimline=true per-customer; fallback to verbose pipeline for customers flagged for full-fidelity retention.
- Instrumentation: track fraction of events with `m` present; aim for <0.1% for normal traffic.

References
- CONFLUENCE-SEC/AE/compact-schema-draft (linked)
- JIRA-SEC-4125: evidence-store retention and TTLs
- PR: platform/pull/1289: initial slimline exporter implementation

Appendix: quick search checklist for on-call
- If investigator says "I can't find an event": confirm whether the path is in slimline topic and if so check evidence index for `ev` id.
- If SIEM alerts missing context: check if `m` blobs were truncated or the consumer pipeline is dropping `ev` field.

End of draft.

(Notes: this doc is intentionally compact — intended to be readable during a runbook read-through. Will expand action token list and add tooling scripts next week. )
